name: Insomnia
tagline: Open-source API client from Kong for debugging, testing and mocking APIs.
bestFor: Developers who want a local-first or Git-synced API client with CLI test runs
description: Insomnia is an API client from Kong with GraphQL and gRPC clients, collection runs, environments and mock servers. The Inso CLI runs tests and linting in CI/CD pipelines, and projects can be stored locally, in Git or in Insomnia's cloud.
pros: Free Essentials plan includes unlimited collection runs and Inso CLI access for CI/CD
Projects can be kept local, synced through Git, or stored in the cloud
Enterprise has a self-serve 14-day trial with no credit card
cons: Mock server requests are capped at 1,000/month on Essentials and 10,000/month on Pro; extra is $10 per 25,000
Git Sync on the free plan is limited to small teams (up to 3 users)
SSO and SCIM require Enterprise at $45 per user/month
freePlanDetails: Essentials: Git Sync projects for up to 3 users, unlimited cloud/local projects, unlimited collection runs, Inso CLI, 1,000 mock requests/month; also a local-only Scratch Pad
trial: 14-day Enterprise trial, no credit card required

plans.name: Pro
plans.notes: Per user; $12 billed monthly, $10 billed annually

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Per user; self-serve up to 50 users, larger teams contact sales; $45 shown under both monthly and annual toggles

name: Katalon Studio
tagline: Test automation tool for web, API, mobile and desktop testing.
bestFor: QA teams that want API tests alongside web and mobile UI tests in one tool
description: Katalon Studio is a test automation IDE that covers web, mobile and API testing, including REST, SOAP and GraphQL requests. Paid plans add headless and CI/CD execution (via Katalon Runtime Engine) with Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, GitLab and Docker.
pros: API, web and mobile tests live in the same project
Supports REST, SOAP 1.1/1.2 and GraphQL requests
Free plan covers local authoring and execution
cons: Free plan has no headless, CI/CD or parallel execution and is limited to 40 static test suites
Professional is sold annually only at $1,800 per seat per year; no monthly price shown
No API mocking or load testing mentioned on the API testing page
freePlanDetails: Local authoring, record and playback, local execution; up to 40 static test suites; no CI/CD or parallel execution

plans.name: Professional
plans.notes: Per seat; '$1,800 / seat / year' (≈ $150/seat/month), annual billing only

name: Apidog
tagline: All-in-one API platform for design, debugging, mocking, testing and documentation.
bestFor: Teams that want API design, mocks, tests and docs in one tool at a low per-user price
description: Apidog combines an API client (HTTP, GraphQL, gRPC, SOAP, WebSocket and more), an OpenAPI designer, mock servers, test scenarios and published documentation. Tests run from the Apidog CLI in Jenkins, GitLab and GitHub Actions, and an on-premises edition is available.
pros: Free plan for up to 4 users includes mocking, unlimited test runs and local performance tests
Paid plans are listed per user with both monthly and annual prices
On-premises and air-gapped deployment available for Enterprise
cons: Free plan caps team projects at 5 and API change history at 7 days
Enterprise is annual-only; SAML SSO and SCIM are only on Enterprise
Cloud mock server limited to 10K calls/month on the Free plan
freePlanDetails: Up to 4 users; API client, mocking, unlimited test/collection runs, local performance tests, Apidog CLI, 5 team projects

sources.label: Apidog docs: Installing and running Apidog CLI

name: Karate
tagline: Open-source framework for API, UI and performance testing, with paid IDE plugins and an enterprise edition.
bestFor: Engineering teams that want code-based API tests in CI without a per-user client fee
description: Karate is an MIT-licensed test framework that covers REST, GraphQL and SOAP API testing, built-in mocks and performance testing through Gatling. Karate Labs sells IDE plugins, Xplorer Premium and an Enterprise edition with async protocol support (Kafka, gRPC, WebSocket) and API coverage reporting.
pros: Core framework is free and MIT-licensed, including mocks, Gatling performance tests and CI/CD use
One framework covers API, UI and performance tests
Paid tiers are listed per user with public prices
cons: Async protocols (Kafka, gRPC, WebSocket) in CI/CD need an Enterprise runtime license
Tests are written in Karate's own DSL, so non-coders need the IDE or Xplorer tooling
Enterprise trials require a vetted, scoped request rather than self-serve sign-up
freePlanDetails: Open-source Karate framework (MIT) plus free tier of Xplorer desktop client

name: Bruno
tagline: Open-source, Git-native API client that stores collections as plain files.
bestFor: Developers who want API collections versioned in Git with no cloud account
description: Bruno is an MIT-licensed desktop API client for HTTP/REST, GraphQL and gRPC that saves collections as files in your repository. The Bruno CLI runs collections in GitHub Actions, Docker and other pipelines, and a local mock server is available in beta.
pros: Open-source edition is free and works without an account
Collections are plain files that live in Git alongside code
Paid tiers are low per-user prices and include a 14-day Ultimate trial with no credit card
cons: Paid plans are listed only with annual billing
Mock server is a beta feature run locally on your machine
SSO and SCIM are Enterprise-only; open-source edition is limited to 2 workspaces and public Git providers
freePlanDetails: Open Source edition: 2 workspaces, public Git providers, 5 OpenAPI syncs/month, unlimited collection runner, community support
trial: 14-day free trial of Ultimate, no credit card required

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Per user/month, billed annually; purchased via Contact Sales

name: Hoppscotch
tagline: Open-source API development platform for REST, GraphQL and realtime APIs, in the browser or self-hosted.
bestFor: Teams that want a free, self-hostable API client with low per-user cloud pricing
description: Hoppscotch is an open-source API client for REST, GraphQL and realtime APIs with collections, environments, pre-request scripts, tests and a collection runner. Paid cloud plans add team workspaces, API mocking and documentation publishing, and the platform can be self-hosted from GitHub.
pros: Free plan covers REST, GraphQL and realtime testing with scripts and a collection runner
Can be self-hosted from the GitHub repository
Cloud plans are low per-user prices with monthly or annual billing
cons: API mocking is only on the paid Business plan
SAML SSO, SCIM and audit logs require Enterprise
No load testing mentioned
freePlanDetails: Free forever: REST, GraphQL and realtime API testing, personal workspace, collections, environments, scripts and tests, collection runner

plans.name: Business
plans.notes: Per user; $8 billed monthly, $6 billed annually

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Per user; $14 billed monthly, $11 billed annually

name: Apache JMeter
tagline: Open-source Java application for load and functional testing of web apps, APIs and other protocols.
bestFor: Teams that need free load testing of HTTP, REST, SOAP and GraphQL endpoints
description: Apache JMeter is an Apache Software Foundation project for load testing and measuring the performance of servers, including HTTP/HTTPS, SOAP/REST web services, JDBC, JMS and FTP. It includes a GraphQL HTTP Request sampler and runs in CI through third-party Maven, Gradle and Jenkins plugins.
pros: Free and open source under the Apache license
Covers load testing across many protocols, not just HTTP
Includes a dedicated GraphQL HTTP Request sampler
cons: CI integration relies on third-party Maven, Gradle and Jenkins plugins
Requires a Java runtime (Java 8+)
No built-in API mocking or hosted cloud service from the project
freePlanDetails: Open source (Apache License 2.0), free download

name: REST Assured
tagline: Open-source Java library for testing REST services.
bestFor: Java teams writing API tests as code alongside JUnit or TestNG
description: REST Assured is an Apache 2.0-licensed Java library with a fluent syntax for sending HTTP requests and asserting on REST responses. It also supports Spring MockMvc and WebTestClient for testing Spring controllers without a running server.
pros: Free and open source under Apache 2.0
Tests are plain Java code, so they run anywhere the build runs
Actively maintained: 7.0.0-RC1 released 2026-11-12
cons: Java only; no GUI for non-programmers
No load testing or GraphQL support mentioned by the project
No hosted collaboration, reporting or mock server features
freePlanDetails: Open source library (Apache 2.0)

name: Beyond Compare
tagline: Desktop file and folder comparison tool with table, text and binary compare.
bestFor: Testers and developers diffing CSV extracts, Excel sheets and text files by hand or by script
description: Beyond Compare from Scooter Software compares and merges folders, text files, tables, binary files and images on Windows, macOS and Linux. Its Table Compare view compares CSV, tab-delimited, HTML tables and Excel worksheets with key-column alignment and numeric/date tolerances, and a script processor and command line allow automated runs.
pros: Table Compare aligns CSV and Excel data on key columns and ignores differences within numeric or date tolerances
One-time license with no annual renewal fee
Runs on Windows, macOS and Linux, with scripting from the command line
cons: It diffs two files; it does not validate files against a schema or rule set
No database connectivity for file-to-database comparison
Major version upgrades are paid (generally half price)
trial: Free evaluation (length not stated on the shop page)

plans.name: Standard (per user)
plans.notes: One-time perpetual license: $35 per user (1-4 users), $28 (5-9), down to $15.75 (100+); site license $5,250; enterprise license $21,000

plans.name: Pro (per user)
plans.notes: One-time perpetual license: $70 per user (1-4 users), $56 (5-9), down to $31.50 (100+); site $10,500; enterprise $42,000

sources.label: Beyond Compare feature list by version

name: iceDQ
tagline: Data testing, reconciliation and monitoring platform from Torana Inc. that checks data across databases, files, APIs and BI reports.
bestFor: Enterprise QA and data teams testing ETL pipelines, migrations and BI reports
description: iceDQ runs validation and reconciliation rules that compare source and target data at row and column level across databases, files, APIs and BI reports, using its own in-memory engine. It is sold as SaaS on AWS or self-managed on-premises, with schedulers, CI/CD hooks and email, Slack or Teams alerts.
pros: Connectors page lists 150+ native and SQL-based connectors, including Snowflake, Databricks, Google BigQuery, SAP HANA, Salesforce, Kafka and mainframe AS400

Tests BI reports against their source data; the BI testing page names Power BI, Tableau, Qlik Sense, MicroStrategy, SAP BusinessObjects and IBM Cognos, and Power BI testing supports XMLA and native DAX queries
File testing covers CSV, JSON, XML, Excel, fixed-width, Parquet, Avro and mainframe EBCDIC/COBOL files, read from S3, ADLS Gen2, Google Cloud Storage, FTP/SFTP and SharePoint
Integrations page lists 20+ pre-built integrations: Jenkins, Bamboo, Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions, Airflow, Autosys, Control-M, Jira, ServiceNow, HP ALM, Xray and Zephyr
Offered as SaaS on AWS or self-managed on-premises; the vendor says the customer controls data access in both
cons: No published prices; the license is described only as consumption-based per user per server or enterprise, and every page leads to 'Book a Demo'
No free plan; the 'Free Trial' card on the homepage links to the demo request form and gives no trial length or terms

Many connectors cost extra: the licensing policy lists JSON, XML, Parquet, Avro, REST API, GraphQL, Salesforce and Kafka as premium data connectors, Power BI, Tableau Cloud and Qlik Cloud as premium BI connectors, and Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions and Jira as premium integrations
For Tableau and Qlik, the connectors page and licensing policy list only Tableau Cloud and Qlik Cloud; Cognos is named on the BI testing page but not in the connector list

Aimed at data teams rather than API developers: there is no load testing or API mocking, and the vendor itself says it checks the data in API responses rather than replacing functional tools like Postman
trial: Free trial offered via demo request (length not stated)

plans.name: Enterprise license
plans.notes: Quote only. Site: 'consumption-based license per user per server or enterprise'. Engines (Standard, High Throughput, Big Data) are sized Mini/Small/Medium/Large; premium connectors and integrations are add-on licenses.

integrations: 150+ connectors; 20+ pre-built integrations
compliance: SOC (AICPA badge, report type not stated)
